reasons: The cited clause grants Customer a one-month convenience exit (better than the fallback notice) but conditions it on uncapped early termination charges specified in Attachment A / Service Option Attachments, with no refund of prepaid charges. An uncapped exit charge fails the fallback's express material term ('early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees'), so classifying this as a deviation rather than an acceptable fallback is defensible and not over-flagging.

The redline follows the rule's redline guidance ('replace penalties with the fallback fee cap'): it leaves the notice period and the absence of an IBM convenience right untouched and adds only the 3-month aggregate cap plus a pro-rata refund of prepaid charges — the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position.

Deterministic failures are heuristic artefacts: the 'Customer convenience termination present' check inspected the edited sub-paragraph p0046 rather than p0044, which plainly contains the Customer convenience right; the 0.633 changed-character ratio simply reflects appending a cap and refund sentence to a very short sub-clause.

Comment is accurate, correctly prefixed, concise, states what changed and why, cites the preferred position and offers to discuss the cap level. Minor drafting nit only: the added refund sentence sits inside a list of Customer conditions ('by: a... and b...'), so it would read more cleanly as a separate sentence after the list.

Severity lowered to medium: the clause already satisfies the preferred notice standard and imposes no Vendor convenience right, and the charges are expressed as 'if any', so the residual exposure is limited to a potentially uncapped exit fee rather than a lost exit right.
